s561.content:
Faith (Foy in French) was a young girl of Agen in Gaul who was martyred for refusing to sacrifice to the pagan gods.

Her relics were later taken to the abbey of Conques, where they are kept in a famous golden reliquary statue, and Conques became a great stop on the pilgrimage road to Santiago de Compostela.
s561.intercession: St. Faith, pray for us. Make our faith strong and joyful. Amen.

s562.content:
According to tradition, Genesius was a Roman actor who performed a play mocking Christian Baptism before the emperor. During the performance he was suddenly converted and declared on stage that he truly believed in Christ.

The emperor had him tortured and beheaded. He is the patron saint of actors.
s562.intercession: St. Genesius, pray for us. Bless all who work in the theater and the arts. Amen.

s563.content:
Giles was a hermit who lived in the forest near Nîmes in southern France. According to legend, a deer kept him company and gave him milk, and when a king’s hunting arrow struck him while he protected her, he was left lame.

The king built him a monastery. Giles is one of the Fourteen Holy Helpers and the patron of people with disabilities.
s563.intercession: St. Giles, pray for us. Help the disabled and all who are excluded. Amen.

s564.content:
According to tradition, Leonard was a Frankish nobleman who became a hermit near Limoges. He obtained from the king the right to free prisoners he judged worthy, and many freed captives came to him.

He became one of the most popular saints of the Middle Ages, the patron of prisoners and of women in labor.
s564.intercession: St. Leonard, pray for us. Free those who are held captive. Amen.

s565.content:
Eligius (Eloi) was a skilled goldsmith who became master of the mint and counselor to the Frankish king Dagobert I. He used his wealth to ransom slaves, often freeing dozens at a time.

He later became bishop of Noyon and preached in Flanders. He is the patron of goldsmiths, metalworkers, and blacksmiths.
s565.intercession: St. Eligius, pray for us. Teach us to use our gifts for the good of others. Amen.

s566.content:
Gall was an Irish monk who traveled to the Continent with St. Columbanus. When Columbanus moved on to Italy, Gall stayed behind as a hermit in the forests of what is now Switzerland.

The abbey that grew up around his hermitage, St. Gallen, became a great center of learning, and its library still holds treasures of medieval manuscripts. According to legend, a bear brought him wood for his fire.
s566.intercession: St. Gall, pray for us. Bless all who study and keep learning alive. Amen.

s567.content:
Fiacre was an Irish hermit who settled near Meaux in France, where he cleared land for a garden and grew vegetables and herbs to feed the poor and heal the sick.

He is the patron saint of gardeners. In Paris, horse-drawn cabs came to be called fiacres after the Hôtel Saint-Fiacre, where they were first hired.
s567.intercession: St. Fiacre, pray for us. Bless gardeners and all who care for the earth. Amen.

s568.content:
Chad was an Anglo-Saxon monk trained by St. Aidan at Lindisfarne. He became bishop of the Mercians, with his seat at Lichfield, and traveled his diocese on foot to preach.

He was known for his humility; when his first appointment as bishop was found irregular, he stepped aside without complaint. He died of plague after only a few years.
s568.intercession: St. Chad, pray for us. Make us humble servants of the Gospel. Amen.

s569.content:
Wilfrid was a bishop of York who championed the Roman calendar and customs at the Synod of Whitby in 664. His forceful character drew him into many conflicts, and he twice appealed to the pope.

During a period of exile he evangelized the pagan South Saxons in Sussex, teaching them to fish during a famine. He founded monasteries at Ripon and Hexham.
s569.intercession: St. Wilfrid, pray for us. Keep us united with the successor of Peter. Amen.

s570.content:
Etheldreda, or Audrey, was an Anglo-Saxon princess who was married twice for political reasons but desired to give her life to God. With her second husband’s eventual consent, she became a nun.

She founded a double monastery at Ely, where she was abbess. Ely Cathedral stands on its site. The word "tawdry" comes from the cheap lace sold at "St. Audrey’s" fairs.
s570.intercession: St. Etheldreda, pray for us. Help us to give our lives wholly to God. Amen.

s571.content:
Swithun was bishop of Winchester and counselor to the kings of Wessex, remembered for his humility and his building of churches and bridges. He asked to be buried outside, where people would walk over his grave and the rain would fall on it.

An old English proverb says that if it rains on St. Swithun’s Day, it will rain for forty days.
s571.intercession: St. Swithun, pray for us. Teach us humility. Amen.

s572.content:
Richard was an Oxford scholar and chancellor who became bishop of Chichester. King Henry III opposed his appointment and seized his property, but Richard lived simply, visiting his people on foot and caring for the poor.

He is remembered for a prayer attributed to him, asking to know Christ more clearly, love him more dearly, and follow him more nearly, day by day.
s572.intercession: St. Richard, pray for us. Help us to know, love, and follow Christ more each day. Amen.

s573.content:
Lioba was an English Benedictine nun and a relative of St. Boniface, who invited her to Germany to help in his mission. She became abbess of Tauberbischofsheim and trained nuns who founded other monasteries.

She was learned, gentle, and widely consulted by bishops and nobles. At Boniface’s request she was buried near him at Fulda.
s573.intercession: St. Lioba, pray for us. Bless all women who spread the Gospel. Amen.

s574.content:
Isidore Bakanja was a young Congolese convert who worked as a servant on a rubber plantation. His overseer hated Christianity and ordered him to stop teaching his fellow workers to pray and to remove his scapular.

When he refused, he was flogged savagely, and he died of his wounds months later, forgiving the man who beat him. He was beatified in 1994.
s574.intercession: Blessed Isidore, pray for us. Help us to forgive those who hurt us. Amen.

s575.content:
Victoria was a noblewoman of Madagascar who became a Catholic against the wishes of her family and remained faithful through a difficult marriage.

When the government expelled all foreign missionaries from 1883 to 1886, she led and protected the Catholic community, keeping churches open and the faithful united. She was beatified in 1989.
s575.intercession: Blessed Victoria, pray for us. Strengthen lay people who keep the faith alive. Amen.

s576.content:
Anuarite was a young Congolese religious sister. During the Simba rebellion in 1964, rebel soldiers seized her community, and a colonel tried to take her as his wife.

She refused, saying she was consecrated to Christ, and he killed her. As she died she forgave him. She was beatified by Pope St. John Paul II in Kinshasa in 1985.
s576.intercession: Blessed Anuarite, pray for us. Help us to stay faithful to Christ in every danger. Amen.

s577.content:
Cyprian Michael Tansi was a Nigerian parish priest who served his people with energy and austerity; among those he influenced was the future Cardinal Francis Arinze.

Later he became a Trappist monk at Mount St. Bernard Abbey in England, hoping to bring monastic life to Africa. He died in England in 1964 and was beatified in Nigeria in 1998.
s577.intercession: Blessed Cyprian, pray for us. Bless the Church in Africa. Amen.

s578.content:
John de Britto was a Portuguese nobleman who became a Jesuit missionary in Madurai in southern India. He adopted the dress, diet, and customs of an Indian ascetic to bring the Gospel to the people.

After converting many, including a local prince, he was beheaded at Oriyur in 1693. He was canonized in 1947.
s578.intercession: St. John de Britto, pray for us. Bless the Church in India. Amen.

s579.content:
Gaspar was a Roman priest who was exiled and imprisoned for refusing to swear allegiance to Napoleon. After his release, he founded the Missionaries of the Precious Blood in 1815.

He preached missions throughout central Italy, including to the bandits of the mountains, and spread devotion to the Precious Blood of Jesus.
s579.intercession: St. Gaspar, pray for us. Help us to trust in the saving Blood of Christ. Amen.

s580.content:
Julie Billiart was a French peasant woman who was paralyzed for more than twenty years, during which she taught the catechism from her bed and hid from revolutionaries.

In 1804 she was healed, and she founded the Sisters of Notre Dame de Namur to educate poor girls. Her favorite saying was, "How good is the good God!"
s580.intercession: St. Julie, pray for us. Help us to trust in the goodness of God. Amen.

s581.content:
Mary Euphrasia joined a community in France devoted to women in difficulty, and in 1835 she founded the Congregation of Our Lady of Charity of the Good Shepherd.

The Good Shepherd Sisters spread rapidly around the world to care for girls and women who were poor, abused, or exploited. She was canonized in 1940.
s581.intercession: St. Mary Euphrasia, pray for us. Protect women and girls in danger. Amen.

s582.content:
Leonard Murialdo was a priest of Turin who devoted himself to poor and working boys during the industrial revolution, directing a college for apprentices.

He founded the Congregation of St. Joseph (the Josephites of Murialdo) to educate young workers and promoted Catholic labor associations. He was canonized in 1970.
s582.intercession: St. Leonard Murialdo, pray for us. Bless young workers and those who teach them. Amen.

s583.content:
Pratulin was a Greek Catholic village in the Podlasie region of present-day Poland, then ruled by the Russian Empire. The tsarist government was forcing the Eastern Catholics of the region to join the Russian Orthodox Church.

On January 24, 1874, the parishioners gathered at their church to keep it from being taken over. When soldiers fired on them, thirteen men were killed, among them Wincenty Lewoniuk, a young husband and father. They died singing hymns, refusing to give up their union with the Catholic Church. Pope St. John Paul II beatified them in 1996.
s583.intercession: Blessed Martyrs of Pratulin, pray for us. Keep all Eastern Catholics faithful to the unity of the Church. Amen.

s584.content:
Clement was a disciple of Sts. Cyril and Methodius in their mission to the Slavs. After Methodius died in 885, his followers were driven out of Moravia, and Clement found refuge in Bulgaria.

The Bulgarian ruler Boris sent him to the region of Ohrid, where he taught thousands of students, translated and wrote sermons in the Slavonic language, and later became a bishop. His school is often credited with shaping the Cyrillic alphabet. He is honored among the Seven Apostles of the Slavs.
s584.intercession: St. Clement of Ohrid, pray for us. Bless all who teach the faith in their people’s own language. Amen.

s585.content:
Naum was, like Clement, a disciple of Sts. Cyril and Methodius who was driven out of Moravia and welcomed in Bulgaria. He taught at the great literary school of Preslav, and then took Clement’s place teaching at Ohrid.

He founded a monastery on the shore of Lake Ohrid, where he is buried. The Monastery of St. Naum still stands there and draws many pilgrims.
s585.intercession: St. Naum, pray for us. Help us to hand on the faith to the next generation. Amen.

s586.content:
Joannicius was a soldier in the Byzantine army who for years accepted the iconoclast teaching of the emperors. After a conversion, he left the army around the age of forty and became a monk and hermit on Mount Olympus in Bithynia.

He became a famous spiritual father, known for his prayer, prophecy, and wise counsel, and he strongly defended the holy icons. He lived to see their veneration restored in 843.
s586.intercession: St. Joannicius, pray for us. Help us to turn back to the truth with our whole heart. Amen.

s587.content:
Theodora was the wife of the Byzantine emperor Theophilus, who persecuted those who venerated icons, though she kept icons in secret. When he died in 842, she became regent for their young son Michael III.

With the help of Patriarch St. Methodius, she called a council that restored the veneration of the holy icons in 843. The Byzantine Churches still celebrate this on the First Sunday of the Great Fast, the Sunday of Orthodoxy.
s587.intercession: St. Theodora, pray for us. Help us to honor Christ, who became visible for our sake. Amen.

s588.content:
Isaac (Sahak in Armenian), a son of St. Nerses the Great, became Catholicos, the chief bishop, of the Armenian Church. Working with St. Mesrop Mashtots, he oversaw the creation of the Armenian alphabet around the year 405.

Together they translated the Bible and the liturgy into Armenian and opened schools, giving the Armenian people their own Christian literature.
s588.intercession: St. Isaac, pray for us. Bless the Armenian people and all who translate the Word of God. Amen.

s589.content:
Paraskevi, whose name means "preparation" and is the Greek word for Friday, was, according to tradition, born to Christian parents near Rome. After their deaths she gave away her goods and traveled preaching Christ.

Tradition says she was tortured under the emperor Antoninus Pius and, after healing the blindness of one of her persecutors, was beheaded. She is one of the most beloved saints of the Greek world and is invoked for the healing of the eyes.
s589.intercession: St. Paraskevi, pray for us. Heal our eyes and open them to see God’s glory. Amen.

s590.content:
Dorotheus was a monk near Gaza, trained by the hermits Barsanuphius and John. He later founded his own monastery, where he taught his monks with gentleness and humor.

His Instructions on the spiritual life are still read in monasteries East and West. In one famous image he asks his monks to picture a circle with God at the center: the closer we come to God, the closer we come to one another.
s590.intercession: St. Dorotheus, pray for us. Draw us closer to God and to one another. Amen.

s591.content:
Barsanuphius was an Egyptian monk who lived as a recluse near Gaza, and John, his disciple, lived as a recluse nearby. They spoke to almost no one face to face, but answered questions brought to them in writing by monks, bishops, and lay people.

More than eight hundred of their letters survive. They give gentle, practical advice on prayer, humility, and daily life, and are treasured as a guide to spiritual direction.
s591.intercession: Sts. Barsanuphius and John, pray for us. Guide all who seek counsel on the way to God. Amen.

s592.content:
According to tradition, Nilus was a high official in Constantinople and a disciple of St. John Chrysostom. He left his career to become a monk on Mount Sinai with his son.

Many writings on prayer and the ascetic life have come down under his name, some of which scholars now credit to Evagrius. He is honored in the East as one of the great teachers of the desert.
s592.intercession: St. Nilus, pray for us. Teach us to pray without distraction. Amen.

s593.content:
According to Armenian tradition, Hripsime and Gayane led a community of consecrated virgins who fled persecution in the Roman Empire and took refuge in Armenia. King Tiridates III wanted to marry Hripsime, and when she refused, he had her and her companions put to death.

Tradition says the king then fell gravely ill and was healed by St. Gregory the Illuminator, after which he was baptized and Armenia became a Christian kingdom. Ancient churches dedicated to them still stand at Vagharshapat.
s593.intercession: Sts. Hripsime and Gayane, pray for us. Make us pure in heart and faithful to Christ. Amen.

s594.content:
Andrey Sheptytsky was a Basilian monk who served as Metropolitan of Lviv, head of the Ukrainian Greek Catholic Church, from 1901 until his death. He renewed Eastern monastic life, founded hospitals and a national museum, and worked tirelessly for Christian unity. The Russians imprisoned him during the First World War.

Under the Nazi occupation he wrote a pastoral letter titled "Thou Shalt Not Kill," and with his brother, Bl. Klymentiy, he hid Jews in monasteries and convents, saving many lives. Pope Francis declared him Venerable in 2015.
s594.intercession: Venerable Andrey, pray for us. Make us brave in protecting the innocent. Amen.

s595.content:
Diadochus was bishop of Photice in Epirus, in present-day Greece, and a defender of the Council of Chalcedon. He wrote One Hundred Chapters on Spiritual Knowledge, a guide to discernment and the love of God.

He taught that the mind should remain continually in the remembrance of the Lord Jesus by calling on his name, and his work was later included in the Philokalia, the great collection of Eastern writings on prayer.
s595.intercession: St. Diadochus, pray for us. Teach us to keep the name of Jesus always in our hearts. Amen.

s596.content:
Kassia was a learned young woman of Constantinople who, according to tradition, was considered as a bride for the emperor Theophilus. She instead founded a monastery, where she served as abbess.

She defended the holy icons and was beaten for it. She is one of the first women composers whose music survives. Her Hymn of Kassiani, about the sinful woman who anointed the feet of Christ, is still sung during Holy Week.
s596.intercession: St. Kassia, pray for us. Teach us to weep for our sins and trust in Christ’s mercy. Amen.

s597.content:
Tryphon was a young goose-herd from Phrygia, in present-day Turkey, known for healing the sick through his prayers. During the persecution of Decius he was arrested, tortured, and beheaded at Nicaea.

He is especially loved in the Balkans and the Slavic lands as a patron of gardeners and vinedressers, and on his feast the vines are blessed.
s597.intercession: St. Tryphon, pray for us. Bless our gardens, fields, and work. Amen.

s598.content:
Porphyrius was born in Thessalonica and lived as a monk in Egypt and near Jerusalem. In 395 he became bishop of Gaza, then still largely pagan, where he worked to spread the faith despite fierce opposition.

According to his Life, traditionally attributed to his deacon Mark, he obtained help from the imperial court to build a great church in the city. The ancient Church of Saint Porphyrius in Gaza City still bears his name.
s598.intercession: St. Porphyrius, pray for us. Bless and protect the Christians of the Holy Land. Amen.

s599.content:
Abercius was a bishop of Hierapolis in Phrygia in the late second century. He composed an inscription for his own tomb describing his journey to Rome and the faith he found everywhere.

In veiled Christian language, it speaks of the Fish, a symbol of Christ, given as food to the faithful with wine and bread. Fragments of it were rediscovered in 1883 and are now in the Vatican Museums, one of the oldest witnesses to Christian faith in the Eucharist.
s599.intercession: St. Abercius, pray for us. Deepen our faith in the Holy Eucharist. Amen.

s600.content:
Khalil Haddad was born in Ghazir, Lebanon, and became a Capuchin friar, taking the name Jacques. Lebanese Catholics know him as Abouna Yaacoub.

He preached across Lebanon and founded the Franciscan Sisters of the Cross of Lebanon in 1930. Together they built hospitals and homes for the elderly, the mentally ill, the disabled, and the abandoned. He was beatified in Beirut in 2008.
s600.intercession: Blessed Jacques, pray for us. Bless Lebanon and all who care for the forgotten. Amen.
